current.text: He is the backup center behind Karl-Anthony Towns and takes over the role Mitchell Robinson played.
Expected to play about 17 minutes a night as the backup center.
He would be the clear starter if Towns misses time and could play around 29 minutes in that case.
The best stash on the Knicks and worth holding in deep leagues. The expert questions his Yahoo ADP of 107.
Knicks big-man depth is very thin, with only Towns and Drummond. Wiseman and Eubanks are in camp, and near the second apron the team will likely add just one of Eubanks, Wiseman or Bradley.
Little double-big lineup use is expected, so his minutes come mostly when Towns sits.

Experts disagree on Knicks rest. Earlier notes expect the team to be cautious with starters' minutes and back-to-backs, mostly over the first 30 or so games. The newest preview says a weaker team in a stronger East may not be able to rest players as much.
The Knicks play a league-minimum 13 back-to-backs, and their fantasy playoff schedule is weak for a season that ends March 28.

durable.text: Still an elite offensive rebounder, a good defensive playmaker and a good screener.
He is older now and can no longer do some of the things he once did.
In a bench role his value is mostly rebounds with few turnovers. Points, threes and assists are well below the pool.

note: Both Yahoo and ESPN value him at 0 USD (ranks 220 and 252), and he went undrafted in our league. With about 17 minutes as Towns's backup and only 6.1 points per game projected, he should not be drafted in a 12-team league. Keep him on the waiver watch list as a Towns handcuff: if Towns misses games he should start, play about 29 minutes and help in rebounds. Early in the season, check which extra big the Knicks sign and whether Drummond's minutes stay near 17.
